messages.subject: Re: [QCA] Error: Incorrect outcome specification.
messages.body_plain:
Dear Adrian, dear all,

I am using the QCA R package by Adrian which is super helpful. However, I am having a similar issue that a previous user (Luc) had with the  the truthTable command in R.
I get the message Error: Incorrect outcome specification. I have tried multiple outcome alternatives from the dataset to see if it works but with all alternatives it returns the same error message. I am using it on a calibrated fuzzy set QCA. Here is a copy of the error message:  truthTable(HEBCCopy, outcome = "ToReConCPD", conditions = "InDeUnEp,
  InDeUnAs, InDeUnCon, InDeUnIns, CStPlBu, CStPlCo, CStIn, CWDeSt,
  CInUbcExp, CTotInGov, CInAcEnCo, CInAcEnBu, CInAcEnPu, CTiAl, CRegen,
  CSST1, CSST2, CSST3")

Error in truthTable(HEBCCopy, outcome = "ToReConCPD", conditions = "InDeUnEp, InDeUnAs, InDeUnCon, InDeUnIns, CStPlBu, CStPlCo, CStIn, CWDeSt, CInUbcExp, CTotInGov, CInAcEnCo, CInAcEnBu, CInAcEnPu, CTiAl, CRegen, CSST1, CSST2, CSST3") : Incorrect outcome specification.

Secondly I am also having an issue with saving/exporting the calibrated version from the Graphical User Interface. I am using windows, I click export but could not find the exported file in the directory.

I would really appreciate your help on this

With warm regards
Habtamu

messages.subject: Re: [QCA] Error: Incorrect outcome specification.
messages.body_plain:
Dear Habtamu,

We need a replicable example (including a test dataset) to figure out what is going on.
At a first sight, your command looks fine, is your outcome "ToReConCPD" a column name in your dataset? (it must be exactly so, with this particular upper-lower case choice).

Otherwise,  the culprit must be within your data. But since this is a rather large truth table (with 18 explanatory conditions), you might want to gradually start from a small one, say using 4-5 conditions, and if everything looks right then step by step introduce new conditions until the error appears.
Chances are you will find something unusual with the latest condition(s) that generated the error.

I hope this helps,
Adrian

messages.subject: Re: [QCA] Outcome column values not recognized
messages.body_plain:
My hunch is that all truth table rows have a consistency score of less than 0.7, hence all entries in the OUT column are 0.  I don't know how large the dataset is, but when you say only 13% of all observations are a member of the outcome, it is plausible that no row achieves a consistency score of 0.7 or more. If you set incl.cut = 0, you should get a truth table as the output with the consistency scores per row in the output. This should help to confirm that all rows are not consistent enough, judged by the threshold of 0.7. You may also set show.cases = TRUE to see how many cases and what cases are in what row.

Regards

Ingo

messages.subject: Re: [QCA] Outcome column values not recognized
messages.body_plain:
I think the issue might be more important than it meets the eye.
Based on previous user experience, I noticed many situations with lots of negative outcome cases, and only a handful of positive outcome cases. This happens quite often when users uncritically collect "samples" of cases, where the outcome is what it is (most cases with negative outcome).

But QCA, as per the original advice from Ragin, is quite the opposite of samples. It is about purposeful selection of cases. While most users think of selecting positive cases, few realise it is also about selecting negative outcome cases. More importantly, the number of positive outcome cases should be roughly equal to the number of negative outcome cases. On top of that, researchers should be intimately familiar with all cases, both positive and negative.

If only 13% of the cases are positive, I wonder if Mayra has in-depth knowledge about all cases. This sort of description (in percentages) is usually associated with quantitative sampling, while QCA is about in-depth knowledge of cases to compare against...

All the best,
Adrian
